passage:
A city's old harbor no longer handled large ships. Modern shipping had moved to a bigger port.
For years, the old harbor was nearly empty. Then the city turned warehouses into museums, workshops, and markets. Fishing boats still used part of the water, and signs explained the harbor's history.
Visitors came for food and views, but many also learned about workers who had carried goods there for generations.
The harbor changed from industry to culture.
Some residents worried it would become only a tourist area. The city had to balance business, memory, and local life.
A place can be renewed without being erased, but only if people protect its story.
